computation_or_rationale: Specialist use and interim timing are resource/timing decisions in the overall strategy (AU-C 300.08); sample sizes, invoices and specific control tests are audit-plan detail (AU-C 300.09).
AU-C 315 risk assessment procedures = inquiry, analytical procedures, observation and inspection; confirmation is a further (substantive) procedure.
Audit plan is more detailed than the overall strategy (AU-C 300.09 vs .08).
AU-C 315 requires analytics as risk assessment procedures; AU-C 520.06 requires them near the end (overall conclusion); substantive analytics optional.
Overstated ending inventory understates COGS and raises GM; understated sales / overstated COGS / understated ending inventory all lower GM.
Slower collection with unchanged terms -> collectibility (allowance valuation) or existence (fictitious AR).
Preliminary engagement activities (AU-C 300.06) incl. evaluating ethics/independence occur at the start; rep letter, overall review and SD communication come at the end.
AU-C 315/240 team discussion: susceptibility of FS to material misstatement incl. fraud.
AU-C 260.11: overview of planned scope and timing, including significant risks identified.
Expected rise not occurring = unexpected relationship -> investigate. Note: 10% headcount x 3% wage = 1.10*1.03 = 13.3% rise, not 'about 10%' as the stem says.
Rooms available x occupancy x ADR is a precise nonfinancial driver-based expectation.
AU-C 300.10: update strategy and plan as necessary as audit progresses; AU-C 315 revise risk assessment.
Slower turnover with stable sales -> inventory build-up -> obsolescence/overstatement (valuation/existence).
AR growing faster than sales with unchanged terms -> existence (fictitious) and valuation (collectibility).
AU-C 300.08: overall strategy sets scope, timing and direction.
AU-C 300.08 / AU-C 620: determine need for an auditor's specialist during planning.
AU-C 600 (extant): component materiality lower than group materiality; SAS 149 term 'component performance materiality' lower than group PM. Lower either way.
AU-C 300.09: plan describes nature, timing and extent of risk assessment and further procedures.
AU-C 510.08: obtain sufficient appropriate evidence about whether opening balances contain misstatements that materially affect current FS.
Interim procedures spread workload and allow early identification of issues; roll-forward needed (AU-C 330.22-.23).
GM = (2,000,000-1,500,000)/2,000,000 = 25% vs 30% expected -> margin too low -> COGS overstated or revenue understated.
Pretax income from continuing ops is common benchmark for profit-oriented entity (rule of thumb, AU-C 320.A8).
AU-C 320.09: performance materiality set at amount(s) less than materiality for FS as a whole.
AU-C 300.08: scope, timing and direction.
Large unexplained GM change with no business change -> possible misstatement to investigate.
AU-C 320.12: revise materiality when info would have caused a different amount; actual PTI 1,200,000 x 5% = 60,000 < 100,000 -> lower.
AU-C 450.08: when accumulated misstatements approach materiality, determine whether strategy/plan need revision -> more procedures (or ask management to correct).
Strategy sets characteristics (framework), reporting objectives/deadlines and scope (AU-C 300.A9 / AS 2101).
Price cut 10% with rising costs should lower margin; unchanged margin = absence of expected change -> possible misstatement.
Reading minutes = inspection used to understand the entity (risk assessment); others are substantive procedures.
AU-C 240.15 / 315: discussion includes how and where FS susceptible to fraud; partner participates; required on all audits.
Planning analytics identify unusual relationships/risks (AU-C 315; AU-C 520 is substantive/final).
AU-C 300.09: plan = nature, timing, extent of further procedures; others are strategy elements (AU-C 300.08).
60,000 > 25,000 threshold
Margin 36% vs industry 30%; cost side tested clean so COS completeness ruled out; DSO 40->60 corroborates fictitious/early revenue
Allowance 5% -> 2% while DSO 40 -> 60
DSI 73 -> 91.3: slow-moving/obsolete stock, NRV write-down risk
